title: Sell Mineral Rights in Frannie, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Frannie, WY | Bighorn Basin
metaDescription: Frannie, WY sits on the historic Frannie oil field straddling Park and Big Horn counties. Get a fair cash offer for your mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Frannie straddles the Park-Big Horn county line, and the town itself takes its name from a field that's been producing oil since the 1920s.
intro: Frannie Field is old Bighorn Basin production, structural traps in the Phosphoria and Tensleep formations that operators found early and have re-worked ever since. Ownership records here run deep, often back to the original homestead patents, and untangling who owns what takes a courthouse visit more often than a phone call.

sections.heading: The Frannie field itself
paragraphs: Like most of the Bighorn Basin's legacy fields, Frannie's production has declined steadily from its early-century peak but hasn't quit. Stripper wells and periodic re-completions keep small volumes moving, mostly under smaller independent operators who picked up the leases after the majors moved on decades ago.

sections.heading: Which county are your minerals actually in
paragraphs: Because the town sits on the county line, mineral owners sometimes aren't sure whether their records are filed in Park County (Cody) or Big Horn County (Basin). Pull your legal description and check both if you're unsure, since it changes which clerk's office holds your deed and lease history.

sections.heading: What buyers look for on a Frannie tract
paragraphs: Current production status, recent decline trend, and whether the tract sits inside an active unit or on the fringe of one. If you've got check stubs, bring the last two or three. If your interest has gone quiet, that's useful information too, it just changes how the offer gets built.

sections.heading: Working across two county courthouses
paragraphs: Because Frannie sits on the county line, some families end up with mineral paperwork split between Park and Big Horn County offices depending on when different tracts were acquired or divided. It's an extra step, but neither office charges to help you locate records once you know your legal description.

faqs.question: Which county clerk handles Frannie mineral records?
faqs.answer: It depends on your exact legal description, either Park County in Cody or Big Horn County in Basin. Check your deed's section, township, and range to confirm.

faqs.question: Is Frannie field still producing?
faqs.answer: Yes, mostly stripper-level production from a field that's been active since the 1920s, operated by independents working the legacy leases.

faqs.question: How does a century of ownership changes affect my sale?
faqs.answer: It mainly means your title chain may run through several probates and transfers. A buyer will want your current deed and, ideally, any prior division orders to move quickly.

faqs.question: What if my deed doesn't specify which county I'm in?
faqs.answer: Older deeds sometimes omit that detail since it wasn't always critical at the time. Cross-referencing your section, township, and range against a current county map will settle it.
